title: Database Schema, Migrations, and Repository Layer
objective: Persist every domain entity in PostgreSQL with pgvector, expose access through a repository abstraction, and provide the indexing needed for the two dominant query patterns: plate lookup and time-windowed per-camera scans.
context_for_agent: The repository interfaces defined here are consumed by nearly every later stage. Design them around the queries the system actually performs (listed in required_query_patterns) rather than as generic CRUD. Keep SQLAlchemy models separate from Pydantic domain models with explicit mapping functions — do not merge them.
required_query_patterns: Find all sightings whose normalized plate exactly equals X, optionally within a time window
Find all sightings whose ambiguity-folded plate equals the folded form of X (fuzzy candidate prefilter)
Find all sightings for camera C between time T1 and T2, ordered by timestamp
Find the K nearest sightings by embedding cosine distance, optionally filtered to a camera set and time window
Find all sightings within a time window across all cameras, ordered by timestamp (trajectory assembly)
Find all match candidates for a target, filtered by review_status
Find sightings older than the retention TTL for purging
Count sightings per camera per hour (for observability dashboards)

tasks.name: SQLAlchemy ORM models
tasks.detail: In src/multicam_tracker/db/orm.py define tables: cameras, camera_links, sightings, targets, match_candidates, trajectories, trajectory_hops, audit_log. Use SQLAlchemy 2.x declarative with Mapped[] annotations. sightings.embedding uses the pgvector Vector(dim) type with dim from settings. Use UUID column types for id fields, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE for all datetimes, and JSONB for flexible metadata columns.

tasks.name: Constraints and referential integrity
tasks.detail: Add: FK sightings.camera_id -> cameras.camera_id (ON DELETE RESTRICT — never orphan a sighting); FK camera_links both ends -> cameras; FK match_candidates.sighting_id -> sightings (ON DELETE CASCADE) and .target_id -> targets (CASCADE); FK trajectory_hops.trajectory_id -> trajectories (CASCADE). CHECK constraints mirroring the model invariants: confidences in [0,1], max_travel_time > min_travel_time, bbox array length 4. Unique constraint on (from_camera_id, to_camera_id) for camera_links. Unique constraint on (target_id, sighting_id) for match_candidates so the same sighting cannot be matched to the same target twice.

tasks.name: Indexes
tasks.detail: Create: btree index on sightings(plate_text_normalized) WHERE plate_text_normalized IS NOT NULL (partial, since many sightings have no plate); btree index on sightings(plate_folded) — a stored generated or trigger-maintained column holding the ambiguity-folded plate for fuzzy prefiltering; composite btree on sightings(camera_id, timestamp_utc); btree on sightings(timestamp_utc) for cross-camera windowed scans; HNSW index on sightings.embedding using vector_cosine_ops with documented m and ef_construction values; btree on match_candidates(target_id, review_status); btree on sightings(created_at) for retention purging. Document in a comment why each index exists and which query pattern it serves.

tasks.name: Alembic migrations
tasks.detail: Initialize Alembic. Write the initial migration creating the vector extension, all tables, constraints, and indexes. Migration must be reversible (working downgrade). Verify that upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade leaves an identical schema. Configure Alembic to read the DSN from Settings rather than a hardcoded URL.

tasks.name: Session management
tasks.detail: In src/multicam_tracker/db/session.py provide an engine factory (with pool settings from config), a sessionmaker, a context-managed session helper that commits on success and rolls back on exception, and a FastAPI-compatible dependency provider. Support both sync and async sessions; choose one as primary and document the choice.

tasks.name: Domain <-> ORM mapping
tasks.detail: In src/multicam_tracker/db/mappers.py implement explicit to_orm(domain_model) and to_domain(orm_row) functions for each entity. Mapping must be total — no silently dropped fields. Include a test-enforced check that the field sets of the domain model and ORM model correspond.

tasks.name: Repository interfaces
tasks.detail: In src/multicam_tracker/db/repositories/ define Protocol interfaces then concrete Postgres implementations: CameraRepository (upsert, get, list_enabled, delete), CameraLinkRepository (upsert, get_links_from, get_link, list_all), SightingRepository (add, add_batch, get, find_by_plate_exact, find_by_plate_folded, find_by_camera_and_window, find_by_window, find_nearest_by_embedding, delete_older_than, count_by_camera_hour), TargetRepository (create, get, list_active, deactivate), MatchRepository (upsert_candidate, list_for_target, update_review_status, bulk_upsert), TrajectoryRepository (save, get, list_for_target).

tasks.name: Batch insertion performance
tasks.detail: add_batch must use a bulk insert path (executemany or COPY) rather than per-row inserts, because the video pipeline in stage 13 will produce thousands of sightings per minute. Include an ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING option keyed on sighting_id so re-processing a video is idempotent.

tasks.name: Retention support
tasks.detail: Implement delete_older_than(cutoff_utc) returning the count deleted, and a companion function returning the thumbnail paths that were deleted so stage 18's purge job can remove the files from disk. Deletion must cascade correctly to match_candidates without violating trajectory integrity — document and test the chosen behavior when a purged sighting belongs to a saved trajectory.

tasks.name: In-memory fake repositories
tasks.detail: Provide fully functional in-memory implementations of every repository Protocol in tests/fixtures/fake_repositories.py. Every later stage's unit tests will use these instead of a database. They must honor the same semantics (ordering, filtering, conflict handling) as the Postgres implementations — this is important enough to be tested by a shared conformance test suite.

tests_substage.description: The critical test here is the conformance suite: one set of behavioral tests run against BOTH the Postgres and in-memory implementations, guaranteeing that unit tests using fakes actually predict production behavior.

cases: each entity round-trips domain -> orm -> domain producing an equal object
field-set correspondence check fails loudly if a field is added to a domain model but not to the ORM model
None-valued optional fields map correctly in both directions
embedding list maps to and from the vector column type without precision loss beyond float32
context manager commits on clean exit
context manager rolls back when the body raises
the original exception propagates rather than being masked by a rollback error
session is closed in both success and failure paths

conformance_tests.description: Parametrized over [PostgresRepository, InMemoryRepository]. Postgres variant marked 'integration' and uses testcontainers; in-memory variant runs as a unit test.
cases: add then get returns an equal sighting
add_batch inserts all rows and returns the correct count
add_batch with a duplicate sighting_id and conflict-ignore enabled inserts only the new rows and does not raise
find_by_plate_exact returns only exact normalized matches and excludes near-misses
find_by_plate_exact with a time window excludes sightings outside the window; boundary instants tested for inclusivity per the documented convention
find_by_plate_folded returns records that differ only by ambiguous character substitutions
find_by_camera_and_window returns results ordered strictly by ascending timestamp
find_by_camera_and_window on a camera with no sightings returns an empty list, not None
find_by_window spanning all cameras returns globally time-ordered results
find_nearest_by_embedding returns results ordered by descending cosine similarity
find_nearest_by_embedding respects the K limit exactly
find_nearest_by_embedding with a camera filter excludes other cameras
find_nearest_by_embedding ignores sightings with NULL embeddings
upsert_candidate updates rather than duplicates on repeat call with the same (target_id, sighting_id)
list_for_target filtered by review_status returns only matching statuses
update_review_status changes only the targeted record
delete_older_than removes exactly the rows before the cutoff and returns the correct count and thumbnail paths
delete_older_than with a cutoff before all data deletes nothing and returns 0
count_by_camera_hour buckets correctly across an hour boundary and across a UTC day boundary
camera FK violation (sighting referencing an unknown camera) raises StorageError, not a raw driver exception
alembic upgrade head on an empty database succeeds
alembic downgrade base then upgrade head reproduces an identical schema (compare via schema introspection)
the vector extension is present after migration
all declared indexes exist after migration, verified by querying pg_indexes
all declared CHECK and FK constraints exist, verified via information_schema

integration_tests.target: constraint enforcement at the database level
cases: inserting a confidence outside [0,1] directly via SQL is rejected by the CHECK constraint
inserting a duplicate camera_link pair is rejected by the unique constraint
deleting a camera that has sightings is rejected by ON DELETE RESTRICT
deleting a target cascades to its match_candidates
inserting 10,000 sightings via add_batch completes within a documented time budget and produces the correct row count
marked 'slow'; the budget is asserted loosely to avoid flakiness on CI hardware
with a seeded set of embeddings, the known-nearest vector is returned first
HNSW index is actually used (verify via EXPLAIN output containing an index scan)
results are consistent between an index scan and a sequential scan on the same data

exit_criteria: Every required_query_pattern is implemented and covered by a conformance test
The conformance suite passes identically against Postgres and in-memory implementations
Migrations are reversible and verified by test
No raw driver exceptions escape the repository layer — all are wrapped in StorageError
In-memory fakes are complete enough that later stages need no database for unit tests
